feed.title: Just 16 Days: Delta Air Lines Schedules 4 Routes To & From Orlando For Peak Holiday Travel
feed.summary: Delta Air Lines is scheduling four point-to-point routes to Orlando International Airport (MCO) for just 16 days during the peak Christmas and New Year travel period, from December 19 to January 3, 2027. These routes connect Orlando with Indianapolis, Kansas City, Nashville, and Pittsburgh, notable because none are Delta hubs. This targeted strategy follows a similar experiment last year, indicating Delta's growing comfort with temporary, non-hub point-to-point flying to capitalize on concentrated seasonal demand, especially for leisure destinations.

feed.title: Eastern Oregon food processor points fingers in nitrate pollution lawsuit
feed.summary: Lamb Weston, an Eastern Oregon food processor, is being sued by residents for alleged nitrate pollution in the Lower Umatilla Basin. In response, Lamb Weston has accused J.R. Simplot Co. and Shearer’s Foods of also contributing to the pollution and has asked the court to include them in the lawsuit, arguing for an equitable share of liability if found at fault. The residents fear this move could complicate and delay their case, which is currently scheduled for a jury trial in June 2027.

feed.title: UAW to Vote on John Deere Contract Extension Sunday
feed.summary: The United Auto Workers union is scheduled to vote on Sunday, August 23, on a two-year contract extension proposed by John Deere. The union's counteroffer significantly exceeds the company's proposal, emphasizing that workers deserve an equal voice in the company's future, especially given the previous month-long strike and the company's strong financial performance. John Deere is optimistic about a turnaround in the agricultural equipment market for 2027 and beyond, viewing 2026 as the bottom of the ag equipment cycle.

feed.title: Culpability of Las Vegas Sands in spotlight as Nevada regulators approve $7.2 million Venetian AML fine
feed.summary: Nevada gaming regulators have approved a $7.2 million fine against the Venetian Resort Las Vegas for anti-money laundering (AML) failures related to illegal bookmaker Mathew Bowyer. This marks the fourth such penalty against a Las Vegas Strip entity for similar issues, bringing the total in fines to $34 million. While the current owner, Apollo Global Management, accepted the fine, most of the misconduct occurred when Las Vegas Sands owned the property, leading to frustrations among commissioners regarding the former owner's accountability.

feed.title: Kraft Mac & Cheese Has Replaced All Disneyland Mac & Cheese, More Details of Heinz Partnership
feed.summary: Disneyland Resort, Walt Disney World Resort, and Disney Cruise Line are partnering with Kraft Heinz, introducing their products across all locations. Kraft Mac & Cheese has replaced all existing mac and cheese dishes at Disneyland, including those at Cozy Cone Motel, and Philadelphia Cream Cheese will replace all cream cheese in recipes and on bagels. Heinz condiment dispensers, featuring standard condiments and Brauhaus Mustard, are also being rolled out.

feed.title: Qualcomm Incorporated Announces Appointment of Sergio Buniac to Executive Vice President, Effective September 2, 2026
feed.summary: Qualcomm Incorporated has announced the appointment of Sergio Buniac as executive vice president and group general manager of Mobile, Compute and Personal AI, effective September 2, 2026. In this role, Buniac will oversee the smartphone, personal computing, smart wearables, and XR businesses, including new AI devices. He joins Qualcomm after over three decades at Motorola, where he most recently served as President of Motorola Devices.

feed.title: JAB Acquisition I to change ticker to ATLQ series after trademark settlement

This change does not affect stock certificates, ownership percentages, or capital structure, and no action is required by current shareholders.

feed.title: Nvidia Reportedly Strikes $7B Licensing And Investment Deal With AI Startup Poolside — NVDA Stock Ends Week 5% Lower
feed.summary: Nvidia has reportedly secured a $7 billion deal with AI startup Poolside, involving $6 billion to license AI models and $1 billion in direct investment, valuing Poolside at $12 billion. The agreement also includes offering employment to over 100 Poolside workers and aims to promote open-source AI and ensure sustained demand for Nvidia's hardware. This move, similar to an earlier deal with Groq, comes amidst regulatory scrutiny over such licensing and talent-acquisition structures.
